top_cited_works.title: Experimental Study of Quadcopter Acoustics and Performance at Static Thrust Conditions
Modeling the dynamics of spring-driven oscillating-foil propulsion
top_cited_works.abstract: In this paper we present a model for oscillating-foil propulsion in which springs are used to transmit forces from the actuators to the foil. The expressions for hydrodynamic force and moment on the foil come from classical, linear, unsteady aerodynamics, and these are coupled to linearized rigid-body mechanics to obtain the complete model for swimming. The model is presented as a low-order set of ordinary differential equations, which makes it suitable for the application of techniques from systems and control theory. The springs serve to reduce energy costs, and we derive explicit expressions for spring constants which are optimal in this sense. However, the use of springs can potentially lead to unstable dynamics. Therefore, we also derive a set of necessary and sufficient conditions for stability. A detailed example is presented in which energy costs for one actuator are reduced by 33%.

recent_works.title: Investigation of noise prediction for a five-bladed propeller under edgewise flow using permeable Ffowcs Williams and Hawkings surfaces
recent_works.abstract: This study presents a computational investigation of far-field propeller noise under edgewise inflow using Detached Eddy Simulation coupled with the Ffowcs–Williams and Hawkings formulation. The primary contribution lies in evaluating and validating surface size—with and without end cap—and end-cap correction strategies for permeable surfaces, along with a theoretical model for optimal end-cap spacing based on equations from jet-noise theory and Spectral Proper Orthogonal Decomposition. To assess these effects, smaller and larger surfaces with open ends, a single end cap, and two correction approaches—JetEnd and SPODEnd—are tested on a five-bladed propeller configuration and compared against experimental measurements. Results show that open-ended permeable surfaces substantially underpredict noise in the downstream region due to vortex leakage, whereas closed-end configurations significantly improve accuracy, with up to 97% of downstream microphones falling within 10 dB of experimental data (vs 33% for open-end). recent_works.title: Correction: A Spectral Proper Orthogonal Decomposition Analysis of Turbulent Flow Around a High-Rise Building
High-Fidelity Simulations of Vertiport Gust Effects on eVTOL Rotor Noise
recent_works.abstract: This study addresses the impact of gusts on the performance and noise generation of an Electric Vertical Take-Off and Landing (eVTOL) rotor. Periodic gusts and turbulence modes derived from building flow wall-modeled LES simulations are applied to a scaled version of the propeller in edgewise flight, influencing performance and noise generation at the propeller. The OpenFOAM solver is utilized to conduct a Delayed Detached-Eddy Simulations (DDES), with the gust generated using a previously developed synthetic-disturbance method. The far-field noise is further calculated using PSU-WOPWOP. The simulations reveal that gust disturbances moderately affect rotor performance, while also altering the spectral characteristics of the radiated noise. In particular, gusts contribute to localized amplification of acoustic sources, which results in an increased overall noise level.

recent_works.title: A Spectral Proper Orthogonal Decomposition Analysis of Turbulent Flow Around a High-Rise Building
recent_works.abstract: This study presents a high-fidelity Large Eddy Simulation (LES) investigation of turbulent flow over a high-aspect-ratio (AR = 7) wall-mounted rectangular cylinder, representative of a vertiport structure, under varying inflow turbulence conditions. A volumetric momentum source term is coupled with a synthetic turbulence generation method to emulate urban atmospheric disturbances with turbulence intensities of 5% and 10%. The effectiveness of this hybrid turbulence modeling approach is validated through power spectral density analysis and comparison with the target von Kármán spectra. Spectral Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (SPOD) is employed to extract coherent structures in the wake, revealing dominant modes at Strouhal numbers St ≈ 0.1, 0.2, and 1.8. A Kelvin–Helmholtz-like shear layer instability near the top of the vertiport is identified as the primary contributor to energetic fluctuations at St ≈ 1.8. The introduction of turbulence disrupts the periodicity and coherence of this structure, resulting in a noticeable reduction in SPOD energy at the dominant flapping frequency, although its spectral signature persists. recent_works.title: Low-Order, Data-Driven Method for Analysis of Impact of Fan Design on Fan Stage Broadband Interaction Noise
recent_works.abstract: Fan blade design plays a crucial role in both fan stage aerodynamic performance and noise. Fast methods for assessing the broadband noise associated with a fan stage can facilitate the design process. This paper presents a two-part study of fan stage broadband interaction noise using a multi-geometry dataset with 59 fan geometries at various operating points. First, a RANS-informed machine learning model for predicting the fan wake flow quantities that are critical to the low-order acoustic model is assessed. Second, correlations that could be used in lieu of even a low-order noise calculation are considered. The downstream fan-stage broadband interaction noise associated with the fans in the dataset is computed using the low-order acoustic model with RANS generated fan wake flow quantities. The results are first viewed as a function of mass flow and total temperature rise as per existing correlations. Next the noise is associated to efficiency through a 5th power of the Mach number downstream of the fan and the 2nd power of the static pressure coefficient across the fan.
